heading: INT. MOONLIGHT LANES BOWLING ALLEY - LEAGUE FINALS - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MOONLIGHT LANES BOWLING ALLEY - LEAGUE FINALS - NIGHT
A cavernous alley.
Neon pins glow over lane eleven.
Rows of folding chairs hold a thinning crowd.
A scoreboard reads 188 to 211.
COACH MAGS DELACROIX, 50s, in a satin team jacket, paces behind the approach with a clipboard she hasn't looked at.
TY, 25, the anchor, chalks his hands.
PAOLO, 19, a rookie in rented shoes, stares at the pins as though they've said something rude.
A STRANGER, 40s, in a camel coat, sits two rows up with a notebook.
He's been there since the fourth frame.
Ty, you're fine. Paolo, you're up.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: I thought Ty was up.
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: I'm not up.
units.name: TY

units.text: You're not up, he's up.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: I'm not ready.
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: You're ready.
units.name: TY

units.text: You're ready.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: I'm so not ready.
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: All three talk at once, an overlapping chorus that goes nowhere.
Paolo steps to the line anyway.
He lets the ball go, and it sails into the gutter with an apologetic thump.
The crowd groans.
Ty closes his eyes.
Mags writes nothing on the clipboard.
The Stranger closes his notebook, stands, and walks down the aisle.
He stops at the rail.
Coach Delacroix. A word.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: After the game.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: It's already after.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She looks at the scoreboard, then at him.
Who are you?
units.name: MAGS

units.text: Felix Landry. Regional development. I've been watching your kid since the second week.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Mine?
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: You. Not the one in the gutter, the one who stayed.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: He stayed?
units.name: TY

units.text: He's been here every night after close. Alone. Rolling the ball into the left gutter, over and over, trying to find where it bends.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Mags turns to Paolo.
He has gone red to the ears.
It bends at the seventh board.
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: You knew that?
units.name: MAGS

units.text: I thought it was cheating.
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: It's not cheating. It's called oil.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: He wasn't supposed to tell you that.
units.name: TY

units.text: I'm not here to tell. I'm here to offer. We take two to the state qualifier. I only need one of you to say yes.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Ty steps up, chalk-white hands open.
Take him.
units.name: TY

units.text: What?
units.name: PAOLO

units.text: Take him. He's got something. I'm just loud.
units.name: TY

units.text: The scoreboard blinks.
Mags sets the clipboard on a chair and, for the first time all night, smiles.
